screening_reasoning: Proposes and evaluates LLM ensembles for automated abstract screening in systematic reviews (INC-01: computational tool for literature screening; INC-02: incorporates multiple LLMs; INC-04: quantitative evaluation with sensitivity, precision, balanced accuracy metrics across 23 Cochrane reviews). No exclusion criteria matched — specifically targets academic systematic review screening, not a pure writing tool (EXC-01), and includes empirical evaluation (not EXC-03).

EligMeta agentic framework for end-to-end clinical trial discovery and eligibility-aware meta-analysis (INC-01: multi-agent pipeline for evidence synthesis; INC-02: hybrid LLM/deterministic architecture; INC-03: deterministic execution layer ensures reproducibility, eligibility alignment as provenance mechanism; INC-04: empirical evaluation on gastric cancer landscape and olaparib meta-analysis with quantitative metrics). No exclusions apply.

AutoConfidenceScore framework for preprint publication prediction in systematic reviews using NLP, semantic embeddings, and LLM-driven evaluations (INC-01: tool for preprint appraisal in evidence synthesis; INC-02: LLM-driven evaluation scores; INC-04: AUROC 0.747, concordance index 0.667). No provenance/hallucination mechanisms described (INC-03 not met). Not a writing tool (EXC-01), domain-specific to systematic reviews (not EXC-02), includes evaluation (not EXC-03).

Evaluates 6 LLMs for full-text methodological assessment of mediation analysis against expert consensus (INC-01: evaluates computational tool for full-text methods extraction; INC-02: multiple LLM families; INC-04: extensive benchmarking with accuracy, F1, AUC, PR-AUC correlations). No explicit provenance/hallucination mitigation (INC-03 not met). Domain-specific to academic literature assessment (not EXC-02), empirical evaluation present (not EXC-03).

Framework for evaluating LLM performance in literature review automation: reference generation, abstract writing, review composition (INC-01: evaluates end-to-end literature review pipeline; INC-02: LLMs for all three tasks; INC-03: explicitly measures hallucination rates in generated references; INC-04: multidimensional evaluation metrics, semantic coverage, factual consistency, public dataset/code). Not a pure writing tool — evaluates the full literature review workflow including reference discovery (not EXC-01).

BioResearcher scenario-guided multi-agent system for translational medicine with versioned playbooks, 30+ tools, claim-level multi-model reconciliation, and provenance preservation (INC-01: multi-agent pipeline for evidence synthesis across literature/trials/patents; INC-02: agentic orchestration with LLMs; INC-03: claim-level reconciliation, versioned playbooks, deterministic execution for audit trails; INC-04: BixBench 89.33%, BaisBench 0.758, clinical benchmark 74.7% hit rate). No exclusions apply.

MedMeta benchmark for LLM meta-analysis conclusion synthesis from medical studies (INC-01: benchmark for evidence synthesis task; INC-02: evaluates LLMs with Golden-RAG and parametric workflows; INC-04: 81 meta-analyses, LLM-as-judge validated r=0.81, stress tests on negated evidence). No explicit provenance/hallucination mitigation mechanisms in the benchmark itself (INC-03 not met). Domain-specific to medical meta-analysis (not EXC-02), empirical benchmark (not EXC-03).

BioInsight provenance-preserving multi-agent orchestration with typed artifact contracts, independent Search Agent, and interactive evidence workspace (INC-01: multi-agent for biomedical evidence synthesis; INC-02: agentic orchestration; INC-03: provenance-preserving architecture, typed artifact contracts, decoupled evidence acquisition; INC-04: evaluation on biomedical QA, protein-function reasoning, end-to-end synthesis with traceability metrics). No exclusions apply.

Experience report on using LLMs for systematic mapping study — describes practical application but proposes no new computational tool/system architecture (INC-01/02 partially met via LLM use for screening/extraction, but no system proposed). Lacks quantitative empirical evaluation of a proposed system or accessible codebase (INC-04 not met). Matches EXC-03: narrative practitioner's view lacking described system architecture or empirical evaluation of a computational artifact.

Proposes PRISMA-DFLLM reporting guideline extension and methodological framework for finetuned LLMs in SLRs (INC-01/02: proposes framework using finetuned LLMs). However, no computational system implementation, architecture specification, or quantitative evaluation provided — only a checklist, roadmap, and conceptual case (INC-03/04 not met). Matches EXC-03: high-level methodological proposal lacking described system architecture or empirical evaluation of a computational artifact.

ARIS autonomous research harness with adversarial multi-agent collaboration (executor/reviewer), three-layer architecture (execution, orchestration, assurance), claim ledger, integrity verification, result-to-claim mapping, claim auditing, and scientific-editing pipeline (INC-01: research harness for autonomous workflows; INC-02: cross-model adversarial agents; INC-03: assurance layer with claim auditing, integrity verification, claim ledger for provenance; INC-04: architecture specification with 65+ skills, MCP integration, deployment experience). No exclusions apply.

MEDSYN benchmark for multimodal evidence synthesis in complex clinical cases (INC-01: benchmark for multi-evidence synthesis task; INC-02: evaluates 18 MLLMs; INC-04: quantitative DDx/FDx metrics, Evidence Sensitivity measure, ablations). Evaluates synthesis of heterogeneous clinical evidence but does not propose provenance/hallucination mechanisms (INC-03 not met). Domain-specific to clinical evidence synthesis (not EXC-02), empirical benchmark (not EXC-03).

AdaMem adaptive memory framework for long-horizon dialogue agents (INC-02: uses LLMs; INC-04: SOTA on LoCoMo/PERSONAMEM benchmarks). However, targets general-purpose dialogue agents, not academic literature discovery/screening/extraction/synthesis (INC-01 not met). Matches EXC-02: general-purpose conversational agent memory system not specifically targeted to academic research or scientific literature workflows.

Educational experience report on software engineering students using LLMs to write research papers (INC-02: students use LLMs). No computational tool for literature workflow proposed (INC-01 not met), no provenance/hallucination mechanisms (INC-03 not met), qualitative analysis only (INC-04 not met). Matches EXC-01: focuses on LLM use for brainstorming, writing refinement, paper authorship — pure writing tool usage. Matches EXC-03: narrative experience report lacking system architecture or empirical evaluation of a computational artifact.

AutoSynthesis end-to-end multi-agent system for automated meta-analysis: search, screen, eligibility, extraction, effect size computation, random-effects meta-analysis, heterogeneity analysis, risk-of-bias assessment, PRISMA-aligned report (INC-01: multi-agent pipeline for full evidence synthesis; INC-02: agentic with LLMs; INC-03: risk-of-bias assessment, transparent PRISMA report, claim-level provenance; INC-04: screened 28+ studies, extracted 20+ quantitative claims, pooled estimates match expert meta-analyses). No exclusions apply.

Qualitative interview study (n=44) on novice researchers' privacy perceptions in LLM-assisted workflows. No computational tool, system, or harness proposed for literature workflow (INC-01 not met), no LLM incorporation in a system (INC-02 not met), no integrity mechanisms (INC-03 not met), qualitative only (INC-04 not met). Matches EXC-03: narrative study lacking computational artifact or system architecture.

Preregistered study comparing human and LLM screening workflows in scoping review (INC-01: evaluates LLM screening workflows for evidence synthesis; INC-02: GPT/Gemini models for title-abstract screening; INC-04: operational recall 82-84%, workload 42-57%, run-to-run consistency 91.7%, file-batch vs all-at-once configurations). No explicit provenance/hallucination mitigation mechanisms (INC-03 not met). Domain-specific to evidence synthesis screening (not EXC-02), empirical evaluation (not EXC-03).

AI Co-Scientist platform for knowledge synthesis with PICOS formalization, relational storage, vector retrieval, Neo4j knowledge graph, hybrid RAG, BERTopic for redundancy/gap detection (INC-01: platform for evidence synthesis; INC-02: transformer/Bi-LSTM classifiers, hybrid vector-graph RAG; INC-04: 95.7% study design accuracy, 87% PICOS compliance, retrieval-augmented outperforms non-retrieval for structured queries). PICOS compliance detection relates to academic integrity but not explicit provenance/hallucination mitigation (INC-03 partially met but not explicit). No exclusions apply.

GRACE-RAG governed retrieval architecture for canonical evidence synthesis: graph-augmented RAG externalizing structural reasoning to retrieval layer, enabling lightweight deployment (INC-01: retrieval architecture for evidence synthesis; INC-02: graph-augmented RAG with Mistral/GPT-OSS/Gemini; INC-03: retrieval-governed architecture resolves structural ambiguity offline, canonical evidence synthesis for provenance; INC-04: experiments across three model capacities, 20% quality gains under mid-scale models). No exclusions apply.

Brain Researcher agentic harness for neuroimaging with rules for admissible analyses, required checks, claim scope, multiverse analyses, scientific review classification (accepted/qualified/revised/blocked/rejected/deferred) (INC-01: agentic research harness for scientific analysis; INC-02: agentic AI with rule-governed workflow; INC-03: rules for admissible analyses, required checks, claim scope limiting, multiverse sensitivity, scientific review as integrity mechanism; INC-04: tool-selection accuracy 23.3%→93.6%, grounding 4.6%→22.0%, collaborator-led studies). No exclusions apply.
